plates.side_label: 1867–2002 TIMELINE · SCHWALBE-LOVÉN TASTE BUDS, HÄNIG-BORING TONGUE MAP MYTH, IKEDA UMAMI & CHAUDHARI-ZUKER-RYBA RECEPTORS
plates.quality_reason: Flow-first: a teach diagram, chart, counter or timeline is a £0 code graphic. No Flow mint.
plates.reference: Own code graphic: on period paper, the 3-era timeline completes: 1867 & 1901–1942 (Gustav Schwalbe and Christian Lovén discover microscopic taste buds, and David Pauli Hänig measures small threshold differences around the tongue that Edwin Boring's 1942 graph accidentally turns into the false textbook Tongue Map) · 25 July 1908, 1913, 1960 & 1974 (Kikunae Ikeda in Tokyo boils 38 kg of konbu kelp down to 30 g of glutamate crystals to discover umami, Kodama and Kuninaka find the 8× nucleotide synergy, and Virginia Collings proves all tastes work across the whole tongue) · 1999–2002 (Nirupa Chaudhari, Charles Zuker, and Nicholas Ryba identify the T1R and T2R taste receptor families, proving T1R1+T1R3 is the dedicated molecular lock for umami).
